newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Small-caps dominate early Singapore shares.
newsitem.headline: Small-caps dominate early Singapore shares.

text.p: Small-capitalised stocks dominated the Singapore stock market trade early on Friday but dealers noted renewed interest in selected blue chip banks and property shares.
At 0215 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was up 7.07 points to 1,927.61 while the UOB blue chip index was up 1.56 points at 877.27.
Among the stocks underpinning the indices were Cycle & Carriage gaining 10 cents to Singapore $12.60 (US$8.63) and Yeo Hiap Seng up 20 cents to S$5.20.
SIA Foreign was also firmer by 20 cents to S$13.30.
"SIA is correcting from recent falls caused by regional currency volatlity," a dealer with a local bank said, adding this was the case for most of the blue chip counters.
The Singapore dollar appeared to be fairly calm hovering around 1.4568/78 to the U.S. dollar in early morning trade.
Asia Food & Properties (AFP) ASPF.SI, Indonesian Sinar Mas Tunggal's rescue vehicle of Amcol Holdings, debuted at a high of US$1.44 before easing towards US$1.27. Volume was active, over 14 million.
Dealers said the sell-off was triggered by a general distaste over the Amcol saga. Amcol was delisted today. One research house valued AFP shares at US$0.97 to US$1.21.
Chinese drug firm Tianjin Zhongxin continued to see keen interest as a "China-play" stock. It was up one cent to US$1.41 on over 6.2 million shares.
Multimedia Creative Technology fell S$1.90 to S$30.90 in line with the overnight fall seen in U.S. technology stocks.
